newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's, Disney expand marketing pact.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's, Disney expand marketing pact.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. and Walt Disney Co., which launched an exclusive 10-year marketing alliance earlier this year, said Friday they have extended their agreement to include more co-branding activities.
As part of the new programme, two McDonald's restaurants will open in Walt Disney World Resort in Florida and another restaurant will open at Disneyland Paris.

McDonald's also will sponsor the Dinoland USA section of Disney's Animal Kingdom theme park in Florida, opening in spring 1998. McDonald's branded food will be served as "Restaurantosaurus," the largest restaurant in Dinoland USA.
Other elements include test-selling of McDonald's french fries at Walt Disney World Resort. At Disneyland Paris, McDonald's also will be the sponsor of the park's railroad.

"As part of our long-term partnership, we are continually looking for fun and meaningful ways to bring our brands together," Dean Barrett, vice president, national marketing, at McDonald's, said in a statement.

The first McDonald's at Walt Disney World Resort is scheduled to open in late 1997 in "Downtown Disney," an entertainment and shopping district. The second is scheduled to open early next year on the main road heading into Disney's Animal Kingdom.
Both restaurants are expected to be company-owned units, a McDonald's spokeswoman said. About 84 percent of McDonald's U.S. restaurants are owned and operated by independent franchisees.

Under the existing marketing alliance, McDonald's has exclusive rights promotions tied to Walt Disney movies. A current promotion at McDonald's restaurants is linked to Disney's "George of the Jungle" live-action movie.
McDonald's, based in Oak Brook, Ill., has more than 20,000 restaurants in 103 countries.
McDonald's stock rose 56 cents to $53.06 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
